payload.claim: The acceptance criterion 'the night names each task it left in flight ... whatever the stop reason, INFRASTRUCTURE included' is not actually met on this path. `_drive`'s in-loop code can append to `in_flight` (line 221) and then, on a *later* candidate, raise from a call `_drive` does not guard (e.g. `ledger.batch_spend`, `ledger.max_run_id`, or `ledger.attach_run_to_batch`, none wrapped in the try at lines 176-197). That exception propagates past `_drive` and is caught only by `run_batch`'s own `finally`, which closes the row `INFRASTRUCTURE` directly via this line, bypassing `_stop` entirely — so none of the `emit(f"{spec_id:<10} left in flight in {state}")` lines for tasks already recorded as in-flight this run are ever printed. The witness for criterion 3/5 (`test_the_breaker_still_reports_infrastructure_over_a_task_left_in_flight`) only exercises the breaker's own `_stop`-mediated INFRASTRUCTURE path, so the `criteria` gate reports this criterion witnessed while this second, unguarded route to the same stop reason silently drops the naming the criterion promises.
